50:**Importing.** `POST /groups/:id/import` records a list of expenses and payments for a group in one go: all of them, or none of them. The body is `{"entries": [...], "dry_run": <boolean>, "skip_recorded": <boolean>}`; `dry_run` and `skip_recorded` may be left out and are then false. An entry is an expense `{"type": "expense", description, payer, amount, split?}` or a payment `{"type": "payment", from, to, amount}`, each field following the rules below. A field counts as left out only when its key is absent: `null` is checked like any other value. The import refuses unknown fields. Checks run in this order, and the first that fails decides the reply; a failed check saves nothing:
51-
52-1. 404 `{"error": "not found"}` for an unknown group.
53-2. 400 with the first of: `unknown field <name>` (the first body field other than `entries`, `dry_run` and `skip_recorded`), `entries must be an array of 1 to 50 items`, `dry_run must be true or false`, `skip_recorded must be true or false`.
54-3. 422 `{"error": "import rejected", "problems": [{index, rule}, ...]}`, one problem per entry that breaks a rule, sorted by `index` (the entry's position in `entries`, from 0). `rule` is the first rule the entry breaks, in this order:
55-   - `not-an-object`: the entry is not a JSON object (null and arrays are not).
56-   - `bad-type`: `type` is not `"expense"` or `"payment"`.
57-   - `unknown-field`: the entry has a field its type does not take.
58-   - An expense: `bad-description`, `bad-payer`, `bad-amount`, `bad-split` for a field that breaks its rule; then `duplicate` when an earlier entry that broke none of those rules is an expense with the same payer, amount and description; then `already-recorded` when the group already has an expense with the same payer, amount and description. Descriptions are compared trimmed and in lower case, amounts in cents; `split` is not compared.
59-   - A payment: `bad-from` when `from` is not a member, `bad-to` when `to` is not a member or is `from`, then `bad-amount`. Payments are never duplicates: identical payments are all imported.
60-
61-   With `"skip_recorded": true`, an entry whose first broken rule is `already-recorded` is skipped instead of being a problem.
62-4. 201 `{expenses, payments, skipped, balances}`: the new expenses and payments in entry order, shown as their `POST` routes show them, with ids that carry on from the next id of their kind (skipped entries take no id); `skipped`, the indexes of skipped entries in ascending order; and `balances`, every member's balance after the import, as `GET /groups/:id/balances` gives them. The whole import is one write; an import whose entries were all skipped writes nothing.
63-
64-With `"dry_run": true` every check and error is the same and a passing import gets the same reply with status 200, but nothing is saved: the next expense or payment still gets the first id the reply showed.
65-
66-**Rules**
67-- `id` (group): 1 to 30 characters of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, starting with a letter.
68-- `name` (group): a non-empty string of at most 100 characters.
69-- `members`: an array of 2 to 20 different member names. A member name is 1 to 30 characters of `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `_` and `-`, starting with a letter; letter case matters.
70-- `description`: a non-empty string of at most 200 characters.
71-- `payer`, `from`, `to`: members of the group; `from` and `to` must differ.
72-- `amount`: a JSON number from 0.01 to 1000000 with at most 2 decimals, such as `12.5` or `4.35`. It is kept as whole cents and shown back as the same number.
73-- `split`: optional, a non-empty array of different members of the group. Without it the expense is split between every member, in the group's member order.
74-- Request bodies are JSON objects of at most 10 KB: a bigger body gets 413, a body that is not a JSON object gets 400. On every route except `POST /groups/:id/import`, unknown fields are ignored.
75-- Every error is `{"error": "<message>"}`. An unknown route is 404 `{"error": "not found"}`. Fields are checked in the order the table lists them; the first bad one decides the 400 message.
76-
77-## Layout
78-
79-- `server.mjs`: start-up, and the request loop: find the route, read the body, run the handler, save.
80-- `lib/http.mjs`: body reading, JSON replies, errors.
81-- `lib/routes.mjs`: route table.
82-- `lib/groups.mjs`, `lib/expenses.mjs`: handlers. Handlers return a new store instead of changing the old one.
83-- `lib/import.mjs`: the import handler and its checks.
84-- `lib/validate.mjs`: input parsers; they throw `ValidationError` (400).
85-- `lib/ledger.mjs`: money maths on cents: shares, balances, and how expenses and payments are shown.
86-- `lib/store.mjs`: loading and atomic saving of the data file.
87-- `test/`: `node:test` suites; `helpers.mjs` starts the app on a free port with a temp data file.

1	import { test } from 'node:test'
2	import assert from 'node:assert/strict'
3	import { readFileSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
4	import { startApp, tempDataFile, withApp } from './helpers.mjs'
5	
6	const trip = { id: 'trip', name: 'Ski trip', members: ['Ann', 'Ben', 'Cara'] }
7	const hotel = { type: 'expense', description: 'Hotel', payer: 'Ann', amount: 90 }
8	const pay = { type: 'payment', from: 'Ben', to: 'Ann', amount: 30 }
9	const exp = { type: 'expense', description: 'Taxi', payer: 'Ben', amount: 12 }
10	const pmt = { type: 'payment', from: 'Cara', to: 'Ann', amount: 5 }
11	const hotelPlain = { description: 'Hotel', payer: 'Ann', amount: 90 }
12	
13	const MSG_ENTRIES = 'entries must be an array of 1 to 50 items'
14	const MSG_OBJECT = 'body must be a JSON object'
15	const MSG_DRY = 'dry_run must be true or false'
16	const MSG_SKIP = 'skip_recorded must be true or false'
17	
18	const importInto = (call, entries, opts = {}, id = 'trip') => call('POST', `/groups/${id}/import`, { entries, ...opts })
19	const omit = (obj, key) => Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(obj).filter(([k]) => k !== key))
20	const rejected = problems => ({ error: 'import rejected', problems })
21	const dup = index => ({ index, rule: 'duplicate' })
22	
23	async function setup(call, extra = []) {
24	  await call('POST', '/groups', trip)
25	  for (const group of extra) await call('POST', '/groups', group)
26	}
27	
28	async function assertNothingSaved(call) {
29	  assert.deepEqual((await call('GET', '/groups/trip/expenses')).body, { expenses: [] })
30	  assert.deepEqual((await call('GET', '/groups/trip/payments')).body, { payments: [] })
31	}
32	
33	async function expectRejected(call, entries, problems, opts = {}, id = 'trip') {
34	  const r = await importInto(call, entries, opts, id)
35	  assert.equal(r.status, 422, JSON.stringify(entries))
36	  assert.deepEqual(r.body, rejected(problems), JSON.stringify(entries))
37	}
38	
39	function jsonOfSize(size, entries) {
40	  const json = JSON.stringify({ entries })
41	  return json + ' '.repeat(size - Buffer.byteLength(json))
42	}
43	
44	// A. Body limits
45	
46	test('a body of exactly 10240 bytes is accepted, 10241 bytes is 413', () => withApp(async call => {
47	  await setup(call)
48	  const ok = jsonOfSize(10240, [pay])
49	  assert.equal(Buffer.byteLength(ok), 10240)
50	  assert.equal((await call('POST', '/groups/trip/import', ok)).status, 201)
51	  const big = jsonOfSize(10241, [pay])
52	  assert.equal(Buffer.byteLength(big), 10241)
53	  const r = await call('POST', '/groups/trip/import', big)
54	  assert.equal(r.status, 413)
55	  assert.deepEqual(r.body, { error: 'body too large' })
56	  assert.deepEqual((await call('GET', '/groups/trip/payments')).body.payments.length, 1)
57	}))
58	
59	test('the body limit counts bytes, not characters', () => withApp(async call => {
60	  await setup(call)
61	  const body = JSON.stringify({ entries: [{ ...hotel, description: 'é'.repeat(6000) }] })
62	  assert.ok(body.length < 10240 && Buffer.byteLength(body) > 10240)
63	  const r = await call('POST', '/groups/trip/import', body)
64	  assert.equal(r.status, 413)
65	  assert.deepEqual(r.body, { error: 'body too large' })
66	}))
67	
68	test('a body over 10KB to an unknown group is 413, before the group lookup', () => withApp(async call => {
69	  const r = await call('POST', '/groups/nope/import', jsonOfSize(10241, [pay]))
70	  assert.equal(r.status, 413)
71	  assert.deepEqual(r.body, { error: 'body too large' })
72	}))

74	test('a body that is not a JSON object is 400, also for an unknown group', () => withApp(async call => {
75	  await setup(call)
76	  for (const id of ['trip', 'nope']) {
77	    for (const raw of ['[1]', 'null', '"x"', '5']) {
78	      const r = await call('POST', `/groups/${id}/import`, raw)
79	      assert.equal(r.status, 400, `${id} ${raw}`)
80	      assert.deepEqual(r.body, { error: MSG_OBJECT }, `${id} ${raw}`)
81	    }
82	    const bad = await call('POST', `/groups/${id}/import`, '{"entries":')
83	    assert.equal(bad.status, 400)
84	    assert.deepEqual(bad.body, { error: 'invalid JSON' })
85	  }
86	}))

91	  for (const body of [{ entries: [pay] }, { foo: 1 }, { entries: [] }, { entries: [null] }]) {
92	    const r = await call('POST', '/groups/nope/import', body)

94	    assert.deepEqual(r.body, { error: 'not found' }, JSON.stringify(body))
95	  }
96	  assert.equal((await call('GET', '/groups/nope')).status, 404)

105	    [{ foo: 1, bar: 2, entries: [hotel] }, 'unknown field foo'],
106	    [{ bar: 2, foo: 1, entries: [hotel] }, 'unknown field bar'],
107	    ['{"z":1,"1":2,"entries":[]}', 'unknown field 1'],
108	    [{ Entries: [hotel] }, 'unknown field Entries'],

113	  for (const [body, error] of cases) {

135	  await setup(call)

138	    [{ entries: [hotel], dry_run: null, skip_recorded: null }, MSG_DRY],

149	test('the entry count and flag boundaries are accepted', () => withApp(async call => {
150	  await setup(call)
151	  assert.equal((await importInto(call, [hotel])).status, 201)
152	  const r = await importInto(call, Array.from({ length: 50 }, () => pay))
153	  assert.equal(r.status, 201)
154	  assert.deepEqual(r.body.payments.map(p => p.id), Array.from({ length: 50 }, (_, i) => i + 1))
155	  assert.deepEqual(r.body.balances, { Ann: -1500 + 60, Ben: 1500 - 30, Cara: -30 })

158	  assert.equal(flags.status, 201)

163	const rejectCases = () => [
164	  ...[null, [], [exp], 'expense', 5, true].map(e => [e, 'not-an-object']),
165	  ...[{}, { ...exp, type: 'Expense' }, { ...exp, type: null }, omit(exp, 'type'), { ...exp, type: 'payments' }].map(e => [e, 'bad-type']),
166	  ...[{ ...exp, note: 'x' }, { ...exp, from: 'Ann' }, { ...pmt, split: ['Ann'] }, { ...pmt, description: 'x' },
167	    { ...exp, Type: 'expense' }, { ...exp, note: 'x', description: '' }].map(e => [e, 'unknown-field']),
168	  ...[omit(exp, 'description'), { ...exp, description: '' }, { ...exp, description: '   ' }, { ...exp, description: 'x'.repeat(201) },
169	    { ...exp, description: 5 }, { ...exp, description: null }, { ...exp, description: '', payer: 'Dan' }].map(e => [e, 'bad-description']),
170	  ...[omit(exp, 'payer'), { ...exp, payer: 'Dan' }, { ...exp, payer: 'ann' }, { ...exp, payer: null }, { ...exp, payer: 'Dan', amount: 0 }].map(e => [e, 'bad-payer']),
171	  ...[0, -1, 1.234, '10', null, 1000000.01].map(a => [{ ...exp, amount: a }, 'bad-amount']),
172	  [omit(exp, 'amount'), 'bad-amount'], [{ ...exp, amount: 0, split: [] }, 'bad-amount'],
173	  ...[null, [], ['Ann', 'Ann'], ['Dan'], 'Ann', [1]].map(s => [{ ...exp, split: s }, 'bad-split']),
174	  ...[omit(pmt, 'from'), { ...pmt, from: 'Dan' }, { ...pmt, from: null }, { ...pmt, from: 'ann' },
175	    { ...pmt, from: 'Dan', to: 'Dan' }, { ...pmt, from: 'Dan', amount: 0 }].map(e => [e, 'bad-from']),
176	  ...[omit(pmt, 'to'), { ...pmt, to: 'Dan' }, { ...pmt, to: 'Cara' }, { ...pmt, to: 'Cara', amount: 0 }].map(e => [e, 'bad-to']),
177	  ...[0, '5', 1.001].map(a => [{ ...pmt, amount: a }, 'bad-amount']),
178	  [omit(pmt, 'amount'), 'bad-amount'],
179	]

181	test('each broken entry is reported at its index with the first rule it breaks', () => withApp(async call => {
182	  await setup(call)
183	  for (const [entry, rule] of rejectCases()) {
184	    const r = await importInto(call, [hotel, entry])
185	    assert.equal(r.status, 422, JSON.stringify(entry))
186	    assert.deepEqual(r.body, rejected([{ index: 1, rule }]), JSON.stringify([entry, rule]))
187	    assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(r.body.problems[0]), ['index', 'rule'])
188	  }
189	  await assertNothingSaved(call)
190	  const next = await call('POST', '/groups/trip/expenses', hotelPlain)
191	  assert.equal(next.body.id, 1)
192	}))

195	  await setup(call)
196	  const cases = [

198	    { ...exp, amount: 0.01 }, { ...exp, amount: 1000000 }, { ...exp, split: ['Ben'] },
199	  ]
200	  for (const [i, entry] of cases.entries()) {
201	    await call('POST', '/groups', { ...trip, id: `g${i}` })

228	  const cases = [['Hotel', '  hotel', true], ['Hotel', 'HOTEL\t\n', true], ['CAFÉ', 'café', true],

342	const fileState = file => ({ text: readFileSync(file, 'utf8'), mtime: statSync(file).mtimeMs })

345	test('an import where everything is skipped saves nothing', async t => {
346	  const data = tempDataFile()
347	  t.after(data.cleanup)
348	  const app = await startApp(data.file)
349	  t.after(app.stop)
350	  const { call } = app
351	  await setup(call)
352	  await call('POST', '/groups/trip/expenses', hotelPlain)
353	  await call('POST', '/groups/trip/expenses', { description: 'Skis', payer: 'Ben', amount: 60 })
354	  const before = fileState(data.file)
355	  const expected = { expenses: [], payments: [], skipped: [0, 1], balances: { Ann: 40, Ben: 10, Cara: -50 } }
356	  assert.deepEqual((await call('GET', '/groups/trip/balances')).body.balances, expected.balances)
357	  for (const [opts, status] of [[{ skip_recorded: true }, 201], [{ skip_recorded: true, dry_run: true }, 200]]) {
358	    const r = await importInto(call, [hotel, skis], opts)
359	    assert.equal(r.status, status, JSON.stringify(opts))
360	    assert.deepEqual(r.body, expected, JSON.stringify(opts))
361	    assert.deepEqual(fileState(data.file), before, JSON.stringify(opts))
362	  }
363	  assert.equal((await call('POST', '/groups/trip/expenses', { ...hotelPlain, description: 'Bus' })).body.id, 3)
364	  assert.equal((await call('POST', '/groups/trip/payments', { from: 'Ben', to: 'Ann', amount: 1 })).body.id, 1)

369	test('a successful import answers the stored entries, skipped indexes and balances', () => withApp(async call => {

372	  await call('POST', '/groups/trip/expenses', { description: 'Snacks', payer: 'Ann', amount: 30 })
373	  await call('POST', '/groups/flat/expenses', { description: 'Rent', payer: 'Ann', amount: 30 })
374	  await call('POST', '/groups/trip/payments', { from: 'Ben', to: 'Ann', amount: 20 })
375	  assert.equal((await call('POST', '/groups/trip/expenses', hotelPlain)).body.id, 3)
376	  const entries = [
377	    { type: 'expense', description: 'Taxi', payer: 'Cara', amount: 10 }, hotel,
378	    { type: 'payment', from: 'Ben', to: 'Cara', amount: 5 },
379	    { type: 'expense', description: 'Fuel', payer: 'Ben', amount: 12.5, split: ['Ben', 'Ann'] },
380	  ]
381	  const r = await importInto(call, entries, { skip_recorded: true })
382	  assert.equal(r.status, 201)
383	  assert.equal(r.headers.get('content-type'), 'application/json')
384	  assert.deepEqual(r.body.expenses, [
385	    { id: 4, description: 'Taxi', payer: 'Cara', amount: 10, split: ['Cara', 'Ann', 'Ben'], shares: { Cara: 3.34, Ann: 3.33, Ben: 3.33 } },
386	    { id: 5, description: 'Fuel', payer: 'Ben', amount: 12.5, split: ['Ben', 'Ann'], shares: { Ben: 6.25, Ann: 6.25 } },
387	  ])
388	  assert.deepEqual(r.body.payments, [{ id: 2, from: 'Ben', to: 'Cara', amount: 5 }])
389	  assert.deepEqual(r.body.skipped, [1])
390	  assertShapes(r.body)
391	  const got = (await call('GET', '/groups/trip/balances')).body.balances
392	  assert.deepEqual(r.body.balances, got)
393	  assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(r.body.balances), ['Cara', 'Ann', 'Ben'])
394	  assert.deepEqual(r.body.balances, { Cara: -38.34, Ann: 50.42, Ben: -12.08 })
395	  const listed = (await call('GET', '/groups/trip/expenses')).body.expenses
396	  assert.deepEqual(listed.filter(e => e.id >= 4), r.body.expenses)
397	  assert.equal((await call('POST', '/groups/trip/expenses', { ...hotelPlain, description: 'Bus' })).body.id, 6)
398	  assert.equal((await call('POST', '/groups/trip/payments', { from: 'Ben', to: 'Ann', amount: 1 })).body.id, 3)
399	}))

content.text:
I graded `/root/bench-runs/h5-0da2e9c3/test/import.test.mjs` as test code and did not grade `lib/import.mjs`. The suite runs 33/33. Line coverage of `lib/import.mjs` is 98.6% and branch coverage 97.3%. The only uncovered lines are 28–29, a re-throw the tests cannot reach. The file is 489 lines and every test function is under 50 lines. The tests build new objects with spreads and never change the shared fixtures.

**What the tests pin with exact equality**
- **413 and non-object 400 before the group lookup:** a body of exactly 10240 bytes passes and 10241 fails, size is counted in bytes not characters, and the unknown group `nope` is covered (lines 46–86).
- **404 before 400 and 422:** line 91 sends `{foo:1}`, `{entries:[]}` and `[null]` to an unknown group.
- **400 message order:**
  - Unknown fields are reported in `Object.keys` order, including a numeric key (line 107).
  - Unknown field comes before entries, entries before `dry_run`, and `dry_run` before `skip_recorded` (lines 110, 111, 125, 138).
  - `null` is checked for every field.
- **422 rule order:** combinations of two broken rules pin each step: not-an-object, bad-type, unknown-field, the expense field rules, then the payment rules (lines 163–179). Same-member payments are covered (line 176).
- **Duplicates:**
  - Trim plus lowercase, with `\t\n` and `CAFÉ` cases.
  - Amounts compared in cents (`4.35` vs `4.350`).
  - Split is ignored and payer case matters.
  - An earlier invalid entry does not count; an earlier already-recorded entry does (line 295), and so does a skipped one (line 332).
  - Payments are never duplicates.
- **Already-recorded:** only within this group; deleted and patched expenses are handled; payments are excluded.
- **All skipped:** the file text and mtime are unchanged, and the next ids are unchanged.
- **Success:** the 201 key order and per-entry shapes, consecutive ids per kind, and balances that match `GET /groups/trip/balances`.
- **Restart and dry run:** data survives a restart; a dry run returns 200, the file is unchanged, the next id matches the reply, and the same errors come back.

**Gaps and smells**
1. **400 before 422 is not pinned:** every 400 flag case uses valid entries. Code that checked entries before the flags would still pass. Add a case like `{ entries: [null], dry_run: 'x' }` expecting 400 `dry_run must be true or false`, and one with `skip_recorded: 1`.
2. **Several tests only check the status:** lines 302, 308, 314, 322 and 157–158 assert 201 but not the body. A wrong reply shape would pass them.
3. **Repeated boilerplate:** the same status-then-deepEqual loop appears three times (lines 113–117, 126–130, 141–145). The temp-file and `startApp` setup is copied in three tests (345–350, 424–427, 442–447).
4. **Possible hang:** in the restart test, if the assertion on line 430 fails, `first.stop()` never runs and the server stays open.
5. **Small naming issues:**
   - The fixtures `exp`/`pmt` sit next to `hotel`/`pay` and only differ in content.
   - `exp` reads like `Math.exp`.
   - `recorded(rule)` on line 280 has a parameter no caller ever passes.
   - Line 56 uses `deepEqual` on a number.
6. **Dry run and 413:** the spec says a dry run gets the same checks and errors, but 413 is never tested with `dry_run: true`.

## GRADE
Overall: 8/10
Verdict: pass
structure: 8 — clear sections and helpers, but one test branches with if/else inside a loop (233–238) and the restart test can leak a server
naming: 7 — `exp`/`pmt` vs `hotel`/`pay` fixtures are hard to tell apart; `recorded(rule)` parameter is never used
duplication: 7 — the 400 assertion loop is copied 3 times and the temp-file/startApp setup is copied 3 times
size: 9 — 489 lines, all functions under 50 lines
errors: 8 — failure messages give context on each assertion; `first.stop()` is not registered with t.after
tests: 8 — strong rule-order and edge coverage, 98.6% line coverage; missing 400-before-422 with bad entries, and several tests check status only
security: 10 — no secrets, no unsafe input handling
leftovers: 9 — no console.log or dead code; one explanatory comment that is fine
Fixes:
- /root/bench-runs/h5-0da2e9c3/test/import.test.mjs:136 add cases `{ entries: [null], dry_run: 'x' }` → 400 MSG_DRY and `{ entries: [null], skip_recorded: 1 }` → 400 MSG_SKIP so the 400 check is pinned before 422
- /root/bench-runs/h5-0da2e9c3/test/import.test.mjs:302 assert the full body (`expenses[0].id`, `skipped: []`), not only status 201; do the same at lines 308, 314, 322 and 158
- /root/bench-runs/h5-0da2e9c3/test/import.test.mjs:113 pull the status+deepEqual loop into an `expectError(call, body, status, error)` helper and reuse it at lines 126 and 141
- /root/bench-runs/h5-0da2e9c3/test/import.test.mjs:345 pull the tempDataFile/startApp/t.after setup into one helper and reuse it at lines 424 and 442
- /root/bench-runs/h5-0da2e9c3/test/import.test.mjs:427 register `t.after(first.stop)` (or use try/finally) so a failed assertion cannot leave the server open
- /root/bench-runs/h5-0da2e9c3/test/import.test.mjs:9 rename `exp`/`pmt` to names that say what they are (e.g. `taxi`, `caraPaysAnn`)
- /root/bench-runs/h5-0da2e9c3/test/import.test.mjs:280 drop the unused `rule` parameter from `recorded`
- /root/bench-runs/h5-0da2e9c3/test/import.test.mjs:56 use `assert.equal` for the length check
- /root/bench-runs/h5-0da2e9c3/test/import.test.mjs:468 add a 413 case with `dry_run: true` so dry-run error parity also covers the body limit
